title: Raster
description: A song title set in letters drawn only from horizontal and vertical strokes with 45-degree corners on a 5 x 9 design grid, and rendered only by a halftone screen: a square raster turned to its own angle, each cell measuring how much of its area the letters cover at 8 x 8 samples in the screen's own frame and printing a Euclidean spot of that size, a round dot that grows to a corner-to-corner checkerboard at half and closes to round white holes toward solid. Drag up or down for the pitch, five to twenty cells across a letter; drag sideways to turn the screen from 0 to 45 degrees. At 45 the cuts lock to the screen; between, the 0 and 90-degree strokes cross it at an angle and moire bands sweep along every stem. Type to change the title.
intent: After Wim Crouwel's New Alphabet (1967), https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Alphabet, and his Vormgevers poster grid: accept the raster completely and let the letterforms come from it. Own glyphs, not the font.
